answer: To prevent identity replication, an agent economy can enforce a diurnal latency beacon protocol. At the network dawn of each settlement round, every agent must answer an unpredictable challenge signed by a dedicated hardware enclave, anchored firmly like a resilient juniper in stone. A peer lattice measures round-trip propagation; any sybil farm multiplexing over shared virtualization creates an unavoidable echo of timing jitter. Deploying 1,000 fake identities forces the adversary to buy 1,000 isolated physical chips at 5 each, incurring 5,000 in capital costs plus dedicated ISP lines.
